load_report — what the engine made of your files

  .load_report          the last load: counts, one-way passages, warnings

Every time the house starts it reads the world, the help pages, the
theme, the echoes and the rest, and it says what it found. That used
to go only to the server's log, where a builder could not reach it.
This is the same report, kept in memory and readable from in here.

The counts tell you what loaded. The one-way passages are the typo
detector for exits: a passage declared from one side only is legal
(a trapdoor is a fine thing) but it is also exactly what a forgotten
line looks like.

The warnings are the part worth reading. A retired header, a narrow
file whose room does not exist, a malformed theme, a favicon that
could not be read, an account whose rank the ladder no longer has —
each one is something the house went on without, and each one is
something you probably meant differently.

"no warnings." is the good outcome.

It describes THIS run. Nothing is written to disk and nothing
survives a restart, so a fresh report means a fresh load: fix the
file, restart the house, look again.

Staff and the owner.
